title: Operating Systems Engineering
description: Build and test the mechanisms behind traps, scheduling, concurrency, virtual memory, devices, filesystems, recovery, and isolation.
overview: Trace one request from user code into an xv6/RISC-V kernel, then extend that kernel through cumulative scheduling, synchronization, virtual-memory, device, and filesystem work. Every mechanism is tied to an invariant, adversarial execution, measurement, and production-system comparison. The 189.5-hour sequence ends in a reproducible kernel capstone and defended engineering argument.

required: C pointers, structs, bit operations, object lifetime, and manual memory management
Stacks, queues, trees, hash tables, asymptotic analysis, and invariants
Registers, calling conventions, privilege, caches, interrupts, the MMU, and the TLB
Git, Make, command-line debugging, and sanitizers
